minutes.headline: Officials warn the FY27 budget leaves almost nothing after health insurance, pointing toward an override
minutes.summary: This was a joint Select Board / Finance Committee / School Committee ("tri-board") session in which the Town Manager walked through preliminary FY27 general government, debt, intergovernmental and revenue figures, including a new assistant town manager position, a large Munis/IT cost increase, and a steep audit-cost jump. The revenue walk-through showed that after health insurance is covered, almost no new money is left to fund any raises, cuts, or level services, and the group spent the second half of the meeting discussing operational efficiencies, the state and federal funding picture, and the likelihood that an override will be needed, without taking any substantive vote.

budget_items.what_was_said: The Town Manager said the select board budget is largely driven by staff covering the assistant town manager, HR/procurement director, executive assistant and minute clerks.

budget_items.topic: Select Board / Town Manager budget increase
budget_items.what_was_said: A modest select board increase was described as mostly expense-driven, while the town manager budget rises substantially due to the new assistant town manager position and a higher legal line.
The Town Manager proposed creating a standalone assistant town manager position, funded for half the year starting January 1, estimated near full-time cost if annualized.
A contracted services line created last year for staff appreciation is proposed to increase to give room for unforeseen contracted needs.
The FY26 accountant budget required a large special town meeting supplement due to transition costs, consultants and hiring, which the Town Manager said should not recur in FY27.
The finance department total was cited while discussing staffing changes including a retirement that offset new hires.
The audit line was said to have been underbudgeted; the actual FY27 audit cost is now expected to be much higher, partly because only two municipal auditors remain in Massachusetts.
Tax title is moving into the operating budget with no change in level funding; a request to restore treasurer/collector staff hours to 40 (from 36) drives a salary increase.

The FY26 IT budget was described as half a million dollars, and the preliminary FY27 IT budget increases further, driven mostly by Munis software costs and a reclassified communications/IT staff position.
The telephone budget line was raised to match actual cell phone and phone system bills, which had been historically underbudgeted.
A large increase to purchase of service is almost entirely Munis-driven; last year's upgrade cost was offset by ARPA which is not available this year, plus a contractual increase.
The on-site IT contractor line reflects five-days-a-week service; the Town Manager has already reduced to four days as of January and hopes to reduce further to three in FY27.
A line covers all townwide phone and cell phone bills across multiple carriers.
The FY27 budget is an election year and salary-driven, with an increase attributed mainly to election costs.
The finance committee's own budget was decreased slightly, while its training/reserve line was kept level from last year.
The salary reserve figure was called premature and not a real number, pending outcomes of active DPW, fire and clerical union negotiations and COLA decisions.

budget_items.topic: Town report / annual meeting booklet printing
budget_items.what_was_said: A large increase in the town report line was explained as covering both the report and the printing of annual/special town meeting booklets, not just the report itself.
Postage was consolidated into one line for the first time last year; it is currently running under budget and may be reduced if the trend holds.
The physicals budget for new hires, including heightened police/fire pre-employment screening, is being raised to align with actual year-to-date spending.
Total debt service is decreasing again in FY27 though by a smaller amount than the prior year's larger drop.
The Worcester County Regional retirement assessment is the main driver in intergovernmental costs and is a non-discretionary increase.

budget_items.topic: Land Use / building department permit revenue
budget_items.what_was_said: Building department fee revenue is projected roughly at recent average levels across permits, plumbing, electrical and gas.
Preliminary total FY27 revenue was presented, described as heavily reliant on property taxes.

budget_items.topic: Levy limit build-up (2.5%, new growth, excluded debt)
budget_items.what_was_said: The levy limit calculation adds the automatic Proposition 2½ increase, estimated new growth, and excluded debt on top before subtracting it back out on the expenditure side.
New growth for FY27 is estimated by the assessors, compared against last year's estimate versus higher actual new growth received.

State aid was presented at the current FY26 actual cherry sheet figure, covering Chapter 70, unrestricted government aid, library funding, school choice and veterans funding, held level pending the Governor's budget.
Local receipts (motor vehicle excise, meals tax, fees, fines, licensing) are being held level pending FY25 closeout, though investment income came in well above projection last year.
State assessments, school choice/library aid pass-throughs and the overlay reserve are subtracted off the top of revenue as non-appropriated, along with a pay-as-you-go capital contribution.

budget_items.topic: New revenue for FY27 and apportionment
budget_items.what_was_said: The remaining new revenue after FY26 appropriations was apportioned traditionally between school, town and Monty Tech by percentage share.

budget_items.topic: Health insurance impact on new revenue
budget_items.what_was_said: Subtracting projected non-discretionary health insurance increases for school and town from new revenue leaves only a small amount for all raises and new costs combined.
The town has been told to budget health insurance at a set percentage increase, which is what was used to reach the small remaining new-revenue figure.
A vehicle stabilization fund exists and part of the FY27 capital plan, including a needed ladder truck, is planned to draw from it.
A fire department budget request for an additional shift was described as not yet included in the presented numbers, at a stated additional cost.
Separate cost figures were cited for funding cost-of-living increases across the town's employee unions.
A finance committee member questioned why the town pays a large annual amount for recycling and suggested it as a possible operational efficiency.
The shared building referred to as TCP/TCPasios was said to cost more annually than the town currently has available in its operating budget.
The Town Manager's working figure for the outer bound of a potential override, before further cuts and efficiencies, was cited from the presentation.

transfers.description: Possible future supplement from the Finance Committee reserve to the Town Accountant budget

decisions.decision: Next tri-board meeting is confirmed for January 27th, to be held in Town Hall rather than the library.
The Town Manager plans to likely terminate the ClearGov software contract this fiscal year unless the incoming finance director wants to keep it.
On-site IT contractor days are being reduced from five to four days a week starting in January, with an eye toward reducing further to three days in FY27.
The Town Manager will meet with all occupants/stakeholders of the shared building (TCP) after receiving the facilities director's report, and plans for a possible winding-down in FY27.
School Committee, Finance Committee and Select Board chairs agreed to send their discussion topics for the next tri-board meeting to the three chairs by Friday.
The group agreed, on an informal poll, to consider adding a public comment period at the next tri-board meeting.
The group agreed a public/override forum should be scheduled, though the date was not set at this meeting.

what_happened.line: Officials said that once health insurance costs are covered, the FY27 budget leaves almost no room for raises, cuts, or level services, pointing toward a tax override.
No vote was taken at this joint Select Board, Finance Committee, and School Committee session.
The audit line was underbudgeted for FY27, with costs expected to rise sharply as only two municipal auditors remain licensed in Massachusetts.
The Town Manager proposed a new, standalone assistant town manager position, to be funded for half of FY27.
The group agreed to hold a separate public forum on a possible override, though no date was set.

why_it_matters: A property tax override would go to voters and would raise bills beyond the state's normal levy cap, and officials here signaled they see it as likely for FY27.
Rising fixed costs -- health insurance, an audit line, IT/Munis software -- absorb new town revenue before it reaches raises, staffing, or school and town services.
A new assistant town manager position is a town-side staffing addition, separate from the school budget rule 11 governs.
